definitions.explanation: Containers or vessels made from clay that are fired at relatively low temperatures, typically without glazing. In archaeology, refers to ancient pottery artifacts.

examples.japanese: {考古学者|こうこがくしゃ}が{古|ふる}い{土器|どき}を{発見|はっけん}した。
{縄文|じょうもん}{土器|どき}は{日本|にほん}の{古代|こだい}{文化|ぶんか}を{示|しめ}している。
examples.english: Jomon pottery shows ancient Japanese culture.

examples.japanese: {博物館|はくぶつかん}で{土器|どき}の{展示|てんじ}を{見|み}た。
examples.english: I saw the pottery exhibition at the museum.

notes:
{土器|どき} refers to unglazed earthenware fired at low temperatures. It is a key term in Japanese archaeology and history. Composed of {土|ど} (earth/soil) + {器|き} (vessel/container).

HISTORICAL TYPES:
- {縄文|じょうもん}{土器|どき}: Jomon pottery (ca. 14,000–300 BCE) — characterized by rope-pattern decorations
- {弥生|やよい}{土器|どき}: Yayoi pottery (ca. 300 BCE–300 CE) — simpler, more functional designs
- {土師器|はじき}: Haji ware (ancient unglazed earthenware)

DISTINCTION FROM SIMILAR TERMS:
- {陶器|とうき}: ceramics, glazed pottery (fired at higher temperatures)
- {磁器|じき}: porcelain (high-temperature, translucent)
- {焼|や}き{物|もの}: pottery (general everyday term)

USAGE:
{土器|どき} appears most often in archaeological and historical contexts. For modern pottery and ceramics, {陶器|とうき} or {焼|や}き{物|もの} is more common.
